title.zh: 卷352 列傳一百三十九 姜晟 金光悌 祖之望 韩崶
title.en: Volume 352 Biographies 139: Jiang Cheng, Jin Guangti, Zu Zhiwang, Han Feng
title.raw: 卷352 列傳一百三十九 姜晟 金光悌 祖之望 韩崶

sentences.zh: 列傳一百三十九

translations.literal: Biographies number one hundred thirty-nine
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 139

sentences.zh: 姜晟金光悌祖之望韓崶

translations.literal: Jiang Cheng, Jin Guangti, Zu Zhiwang, Han Feng
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cheng, Jin Guangti, Zu Zhiwang, and Han Feng

sentences.zh: 姜晟，字光宇，江蘇元和人。

translations.literal: Jiang Cheng, courtesy name Guangyu, was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cheng, whose courtesy name was Guangyu, came from Yuanhe in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，授刑部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, and was promoted successively to director.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1766, entered the Ministry of Punishments as a principal secretary, and rose step by step to director.

sentences.zh: 擢光祿寺少卿，轉太僕寺，仍兼刑部行走。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud, while still serving concurrently in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud, he continued to hold concurrent duty in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，出為江西按察使。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he went out to serve as Jiangxi provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 he was appointed provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 逾年，超擢刑部侍郎，屢命赴各省按事讞獄。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted out of turn to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and was repeatedly ordered to go to the provinces to investigate cases and review criminal judgments.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted ahead of schedule to vice minister of punishments and was often sent to the provinces to investigate affairs and review capital cases.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，授湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was appointed governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 he was made governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 時大軍徵台灣，晟運米十萬石濟餉需，上嘉之，予議敘。

translations.literal: At that time the great army was campaigning against Taiwan; Cheng transported one hundred thousand shi of grain to meet pay and provisions needs. The emperor praised this and granted him consideration for merit-based promotion.
translations.idiomatic: While the main forces were campaigning in Taiwan, he shipped a hundred thousand shi of rice to cover army rations. The throne commended him and recommended him for a merit citation.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，荊州江堤潰，命大學士阿桂等往勘，以晟未能疏濬上游漲沙，並坐屬吏婪索淮鹽匣費，褫頂帶。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year the Jiangzhou river dike burst. The emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui and others to go and survey the damage. Cheng was held responsible for failing to dredge the upstream silt buildup, and also implicated because subordinates had extorted Huai salt chest fees; his official insignia were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1788 the Jingzhou river embankment collapsed. Grand Secretary Agui and others were sent to inspect the breach. Cheng was blamed for not clearing the silt that had built up upstream and also for subordinates who had extorted fees on Huai salt transport chests; he was stripped of his rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋召授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and reappointed vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，復出為湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he again went out as governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1791 he was again posted as governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 芷江境失餉鞘久不獲，晟捕首犯置之法。

translations.literal: In Zhijiang territory a lost pay convoy had long gone unrecovered; Cheng captured the chief culprit and had him executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When a military pay convoy was lost in Zhijiang and the case had long gone unsolved, he seized the ringleader and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 洞庭湖盜董舒友等積年為商旅害，邏獲之，傳首湖幹，盜風以靖。

translations.literal: The Dongting Lake bandits Dong Shuyou and others had for years harmed merchants and travelers; Cheng soon captured them, displayed their heads along the lakeshore, and banditry was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shuyou and his gang on Dongting Lake had preyed on travelers for years. Cheng captured them quickly, exposed their heads along the shore, and piracy on the lake subsided.

sentences.zh: 六十年，黔苗石柳鄧叛，永綏苗石三保應之，晟偕總督畢沅往剿。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the Qian Miao leader Shi Liudeng rebelled, and the Yongshui Miao leader Shi Sanbao rose in response; Cheng went with Governor-General Bi Yuan to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 the Qian Miao chieftain Shi Liudeng rebelled, and the Yongshui Miao chieftain Shi Sanbao joined him. Cheng marched with Governor-General Bi Yuan to suppress the uprising.

sentences.zh: 尋雲貴總督福康安來督師，晟駐辰州治軍需，分兵屯諸要隘，緝獲姦匪百戶楊國安父子解京，詔嘉其治軍鎮靜，下部議敘。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yun-Gui Governor-General Fukang'an came to take command of the army. Cheng remained at Chenzhou to manage military supplies, divided troops to garrison the key passes, and arrested and sent to the capital the traitor-bandit hundred-household head Yang Guo'an and his son. An edict praised his calm management of the army, and the ministry was ordered to consider him for merit promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Fukang'an of Yunnan-Guizhou arrived to take command, Cheng stayed at Chenzhou to handle logistics, posted troops at the critical passes, and sent the collaborator Yang Guo'an and his son to Beijing in chains. The court praised his steady conduct of the campaign and referred his case for a merit citation.

sentences.zh: 三月，赴鎮筸查緝邊備，並撫難民，上以辰州要衝，命仍回駐。

translations.literal: In the third month he went to Zhenqian to inspect border defense and pacify refugees. Because Chenzhou was a strategic point, the emperor ordered him to return and remain stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he went to Zhenqian to inspect the frontier and relieve refugees. The emperor, judging Chenzhou the vital hinge of the campaign, ordered him back to his post there.

sentences.zh: 首逆吳半生就獲，予優敘。

translations.literal: When the chief rebel Wu Bansheng was captured, Cheng was granted exceptional consideration for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: After the chief rebel Wu Bansheng was taken, he received an exceptional merit citation.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，湖北枝江、來鳳邪匪起，遣副將慶溥擊賊於龍山，走之，湖南境內獲安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, heterodox bandits rose in Zhijiang and Laifeng in Hubei. He sent Deputy Commander Qing Pu to strike the rebels at Longshan, drove them off, and peace was restored within Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796 sectarian rebels broke out in Zhijiang and Laifeng in Hubei. He sent Deputy Commander Qing Pu to defeat them at Longshan and drive them out, and Hunan was secured.

sentences.zh: 是年，福康安、和琳先後卒於軍，晟偕額勒登保、德楞泰等剿撫，加總督銜。

translations.literal: That year Fukang'an and Helin died in succession at the front. Cheng joined Eledengbao, Delengtai, and others in suppression and pacification, and was given the rank of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fukang'an and Helin died one after another in camp. Cheng worked with Eledengbao, Delengtai, and others to suppress and pacify the rebels, and was given governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 苗疆漸平，駐辰州治善後事宜。

translations.literal: As the Miao frontier gradually quieted, he remained at Chenzhou to handle postwar affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As the Miao country slowly settled, he stayed at Chenzhou to manage reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼署總督。

translations.literal: In the second year he also served as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797 he served additionally as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 三年，京察，予議敘。

translations.literal: In the third year, at the capital personnel review, he was granted consideration for merit promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1798, at the metropolitan performance review, he was recommended for a merit citation.

sentences.zh: 布政使鄭源鸘附和珅，以貪著，需索屬吏，必多金始得赴任。

translations.literal: Provincial treasurer Zheng Yuanluan was attached to Heshen and was notorious for greed; he demanded payment from subordinates, who had to offer large sums of gold before they could take up their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial treasurer Zheng Yuanluan, a follower of Heshen, was notorious for corruption. He extorted his subordinates and would not let them take office until they paid him heavily in gold.

sentences.zh: 屬吏藉胥役為幹辦，縱今哧詐浮收，苦累百姓。

translations.literal: Subordinates relied on clerks and runners as agents, allowed them to intimidate and extort with inflated collections, and thus oppressed the people.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates used clerks and runners as fixers, letting them bully the people with padded levies until the common folk were ground down.

sentences.zh: 四年，和珅敗，為言官論劾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Heshen fell, censorial officials impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799, after Heshen's downfall, censors brought charges against him.

sentences.zh: 詔「晟平日居官猶能自守，因畏和珅不敢參劾，尚非通同舞弊」，命逮訊源鸘，籍其貲財，澈底根究，具得源鸘加扣平餘、蓄養優伶、眷屬多至三百人諸罪狀，論大辟；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Cheng in his usual conduct of office could still keep himself clean; because he feared Heshen he did not impeach him, yet this was still not collusion in fraud." The emperor ordered Yuanluan arrested and interrogated, his property registered and confiscated, and a thorough investigation made. All charges were established, including Yuanluan's extra deductions from surplus grain balances, keeping of actors, and dependents numbering as many as three hundred persons; he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ruled that Cheng had generally kept his hands clean but, fearing Heshen, had failed to denounce him—yet this was not treated as outright collusion. Yuanluan was arrested, his goods confiscated, and a full inquiry pursued. He was found guilty of skimming surplus grain accounts, keeping a troupe of actors, and maintaining a household of nearly three hundred dependents, and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 晟坐失察，當革職留任，上特寬之。

translations.literal: Cheng was punished for failure of supervision and should have been dismissed yet retained in office; the emperor specially showed him leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was held negligent and liable to dismissal with retention in post, but the emperor specially spared him.

sentences.zh: 冬，鎮筸苗吳陳受倡亂，晟督師守隘，同知傅鼐以計擒斬之，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In winter the Zhenqian Miao leader Wu Chenshou incited rebellion. Cheng directed the army in guarding the passes; subprefect Fu Nai captured and executed him by stratagem. Cheng was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Zhenqian Miao chieftain Wu Chenshou raised a revolt. Cheng held the passes while Subprefect Fu Nai trapped and killed him. Cheng was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，實授總督，尋調直隸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was formally appointed governor-general, and soon afterward was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 he received a regular appointment as governor-general and was soon transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 六年，畿輔久雨，永定河決。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the capital region had long rains and the Yongding River burst its banks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 prolonged rains in the metropolitan district caused the Yongding River to break.

sentences.zh: 坐奏報遲延，褫職逮問，發河工效力。

translations.literal: Because his memorial reports were delayed, he was stripped of office, arrested and interrogated, and sent to serve on river works at reduced rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of rank, arrested, and sent to labor on river works for reporting too slowly.

sentences.zh: 工竣，予主事銜，刑部行走。

translations.literal: When the works were completed he was given the rank of principal secretary and concurrent service in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the project ended he was restored to principal-secretary rank with concurrent duty in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 七年，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he was again made vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 晟自為曹郎，以治獄明慎受知高宗，易攵歷中外，至是凡三入佐刑部。

translations.literal: From the time Cheng served as a bureau secretary, his clear and careful handling of criminal cases won the esteem of the Gaozong Emperor. He served in posts both within the capital and in the provinces, and by this point had entered the Ministry of Punishments as assistant minister three times.
translations.idiomatic: From his days as a bureau secretary, his careful and lucid handling of criminal cases had won Qianlong's trust. He had served widely in the capital and in the provinces, and by now had entered the Ministry of Punishments as its second-in-command three times.

sentences.zh: 仁宗尤重刑事，晟讞鞫務得其平，多平反者。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor especially valued criminal matters; in reviewing and trying cases Cheng strove to reach fair judgments, and many were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing placed special weight on criminal justice. Cheng reviewed cases with an eye to fairness, and many wrongful convictions were overturned.

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫張誠基剿義寧州匪，飾稱自率兵臨陣，為屬吏所訐。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Governor Zhang Chengji suppressed bandits in Yining Prefecture but falsely claimed that he personally led troops into battle, and was impeached by a subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi Governor Zhang Chengji suppressed bandits in Yining, he falsely claimed to have led the troops in person, and a subordinate exposed him.

sentences.zh: 命晟往按，得實，逮誠基，遂暫署巡撫。

translations.literal: Cheng was ordered to go and investigate; the facts were established, Zhang Chengji was arrested, and Cheng then temporarily served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was sent to investigate, confirmed the charge, had Zhang arrested, and briefly acted as governor himself.

sentences.zh: 尋回京。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 九年，兼署戶部侍郎，命赴南河查勘清口運道，疏言河身淤墊，黃水增高，致清水不能暢注，宜啟祥符五瑞等閘以減黃，增運口蓋壩以蓄清，如議行。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he also served as acting vice minister of Revenue and was ordered to go to the Southern Canal to survey the Qingkou transport route. In a memorial he said the river channel was silted and raised, the Yellow River water had risen higher, and clear water could not flow freely; the Xiangfu and Wurui sluice gates should be opened to reduce the Yellow River flow, and the transport mouth cover dam should be increased to store clear water. His proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 he served additionally as acting vice minister of revenue and was sent to inspect the Qingkou transport channel on the Southern Canal. He reported that silting had raised the bed, the Yellow River had risen, and clear water could no longer run freely. He proposed opening the Xiangfu and Wurui gates to bleed off Yellow River water and raising the cover dam at the transport mouth to hold clear water. The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以老疾乞休，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, citing age and illness, he requested retirement; a warm edict urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806, pleading age and illness, he asked to retire, but a gracious edict urged him to stay on.

sentences.zh: 以刑部事繁，特調工部。

translations.literal: Because the Ministry of Punishments was overburdened with business, he was specially transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Ministry of Punishments was overburdened, he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 章再上，乃命解職在京養疴。

translations.literal: When he memorialized again, he was ordered to leave office and convalesce in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he memorialized again, he was released from office to recover his health in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 尋以前在直隸失察籓庫虛收事，降四品京堂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because of his earlier failure in Zhili to detect false receipts in the princely storehouse, he was reduced to a fourth-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted to fourth-rank capital official for an earlier failure in Zhili to uncover false entries in a princely treasury.

sentences.zh: 歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He returned home and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and died there.

sentences.zh: 金光悌，字蘭畦，安徽英山人。

translations.literal: Jin Guangti, courtesy name Lanqi, was a native of Yingshan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guangti, whose courtesy name was Lanqi, came from Yingshan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 由舉人授內閣中書。

translations.literal: From juren status he was appointed a Secretariat drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he was appointed a Grand Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年，成進士，轉宗人府主事。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was transferred to principal secretary in the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1780 and was transferred to the Court of the Imperial Clan as principal secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部員外郎，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was moved to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments and served successively as director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments and then to director.

sentences.zh: 截取京察，並當外任，仍留部。

translations.literal: At the special capital review he was also eligible for provincial appointment, yet he remained in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: At a special metropolitan review he was eligible for a provincial post, but he remained in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，部臣奏請以四品京堂用，允之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year ministry officials memorialized that he should be used as a fourth-rank capital official; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 the ministry recommended him for a fourth-rank capital post, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 江西舉人彭良馵為子賄買吏員執照，光悌與為姻親，御史初彭齡劾光悌瞻徇，坐降調，仍補刑部員外郎，留部覈辦秋審。

translations.literal: Jiangxi juren Peng Liangfu bribed to buy an official license for his son. Guangti was related to him by marriage. Censor Chu Pengling impeached Guangti for favoritism; he was punished with demotion and transfer, but was still reappointed vice director in the Ministry of Punishments and kept in the ministry to handle the autumn review of capital cases.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi graduate Peng Liangfu bought an official license for his son by bribery, Guangti, who was related to him by marriage, was impeached by Censor Chu Pengling for showing favor. He was demoted but kept on in the ministry as vice director to handle the autumn capital-case review.

sentences.zh: 御史張鵬展复劾之，詔：「光悌在部久，平日毀多譽少，停其兼部。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Pengzhan impeached him again. An edict said: "Guangti has been in the ministry a long time; in ordinary times blame for him is many and praise few. Stop his concurrent ministry duties."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Pengzhan impeached him again. The throne ruled: "Guangti has been in the ministry for years and is more often criticized than praised. Suspend his concurrent duties in the ministry."

sentences.zh: 」尋兼內閣侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he also served as a Hanlin Reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent appointment as Hanlin Reader in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年，授山東按察使，晉布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he was appointed Shandong provincial judicial commissioner and was promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he was made judicial commissioner of Shandong and then promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十年，召授刑部侍郎，數奉使赴山東、直隸、天津、熱河勘獄，並得實以報。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recalled and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments. He was repeatedly sent on missions to Shandong, Zhili, Tianjin, and Rehe to investigate criminal cases, and in each case reported the facts accurately.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he was recalled as vice minister of punishments and repeatedly sent to Shandong, Zhili, Tianjin, and Rehe to investigate cases, each time reporting what he found with accuracy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806 he was appointed governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 疏言江西積案繁多，請設局清釐。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said Jiangxi had many accumulated cases and requested that a bureau be established to clear them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Jiangxi was burdened with a backlog of cases and asked to set up a bureau to clear them.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1809 he was promoted to minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 光悌自居郎曹，為長官所倚，至是益自力。

translations.literal: From the time Guangti served in the bureau offices he had been relied on by his superiors; by this point he exerted himself all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From his years in the bureau he had been trusted by his superiors, and as minister he drove himself harder still.

sentences.zh: 以當時讞獄多以寬厚為福，往往稍減罪狀上之，部臣懸千里推鞫，苟引律當毋更議。

translations.literal: Because at that time criminal judgments often treated leniency as a blessing, officials frequently submitted slightly reduced charges. Ministry officials, though cases might be referred a thousand li away for retrial, would hold that if the cited statute was appropriate there should be no further discussion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many treated leniency in capital cases as a virtue and routinely shaved down the charges. Even when a case was sent a thousand li for retrial, ministry officials would say that if the statute cited fit, no further debate was needed.

sentences.zh: 故遇事必持律，不得減比。

translations.literal: Therefore in every matter he insisted on the statutes and would not permit reduction by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: Guangti, by contrast, insisted on the letter of the law and would not allow charges to be reduced by analogy.

sentences.zh: 人咸以光悌用法嚴，然亦有從寬者。

translations.literal: People all regarded Guangti as strict in applying the law, yet there were also cases in which he showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He had a reputation for severity, yet he could be lenient as well.

sentences.zh: 舊例，監守自盜限內完贓者減等，乾隆二十六年改重不減等，光悌奏復舊例。

translations.literal: By old precedent, when custodians who stole what they guarded made restitution within the time limit, the penalty was reduced one degree. In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong this was changed to a heavier penalty without reduction. Guangti memorialized to restore the old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, a custodian who stole official property could have his sentence reduced if he made restitution in time. In 1761 that leniency was abolished. Guangti memorialized to restore the earlier practice.

sentences.zh: 後阿克蘇錢局章京盜官錢，計贓五百兩以上，主者引平人竊盜律，當絞情實。

translations.literal: Later a Aksu mint clerk stole official money amounting to more than five hundred taels. The official in charge cited the statute on theft by common persons and sentenced him to strangulation after review.
translations.idiomatic: Later a clerk at the Aksu mint stole more than five hundred taels of government money. The responsible official applied the common-theft statute and recommended strangulation after review.

sentences.zh: 光悌曰：「盜官錢當擬斬監追，不決，絞情實則決矣。

translations.literal: Guangti said: "Stealing official money should be sentenced to beheading after imprisonment with reprieve; it is not to be carried out at once. If sentenced to strangulation after review, it would be carried out immediately."
translations.idiomatic: Guangti said: "Theft of government funds should be sentenced to beheading after imprisonment with reprieve, which is not immediately executed. Strangulation after review would be carried out at once."

sentences.zh: 不得引竊盜律。

translations.literal: The statute on common theft must not be cited.
translations.idiomatic: The common-theft statute must not be applied.

sentences.zh: 」奏平之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to have the sentence reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a lighter sentence.

sentences.zh: 仁宗覽奏曰：「官盜較私盜反薄耶？

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor read the memorial he said: "Is theft of official property treated more lightly than private theft?"
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, Jiaqing asked: "So theft of public funds is punished more lightly than private theft?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「與其有聚斂之臣，寧有盜臣。

translations.literal: He replied: "Better to have a thieving minister than a minister who amasses wealth by extortion."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Better a thief in office than an extortioner."

sentences.zh: 律意如是。

translations.literal: Such is the intent of the law.
translations.idiomatic: That is what the law intends.

sentences.zh: 」卒如其議。

translations.literal: In the end the case was decided according to his view.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the court adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 光悌練習律例，議必堅執，同列無以奪之。

translations.literal: Guangti was thoroughly versed in statutes and precedents; in discussion he always held firmly to his position, and his colleagues could not overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in statutes and precedents, he held his ground in debate, and his colleagues could not budge him.

sentences.zh: 然屢被彈劾，時論亦不盡以為平允。

translations.literal: Yet he was repeatedly impeached, and contemporary opinion did not entirely regard him as fair.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was impeached again and again, and opinion at the time did not wholly consider him evenhanded.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於官，詔依尚書例賜卹。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died in office; an edict granted posthumous favors according to the precedent for ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1812 he died in office, and the court granted posthumous honors appropriate to a minister.

sentences.zh: 祖之望，字舫齋，福建浦城人。

translations.literal: Zu Zhiwang, courtesy name Fangzhai, was a native of Pucheng in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Zhiwang, whose courtesy name was Fangzhai, came from Pucheng in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年進士，選庶吉士，散館授刑部主事，洊升郎中。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and after leaving the academy was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, then was promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in 1778, entered the Hanlin Academy, and on leaving was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, rising step by step to director.

sentences.zh: 俸滿當截取外任，以諳悉部務留之。

translations.literal: When his term of service was complete he was due for selection for provincial appointment, but because he was thoroughly familiar with ministry affairs he was kept in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was eligible for a provincial post, but his mastery of ministry business kept him in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 京察一等，以四五品京堂用。

translations.literal: At the capital review he received the top grade and was recommended for use as a fourth- or fifth-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: At the metropolitan review he received the top grade and was marked for a fourth- or fifth-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 歷通政司參議、太常寺少卿，仍兼部務。

translations.literal: He served successively as counselor in the Office of Transmission and as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, while still holding concurrent ministry duties.
translations.idiomatic: He served as counselor in the Office of Transmission and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining concurrent duty in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，出為山西按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he went out as Shanxi provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1793 he was posted as judicial commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 摘律例民間易犯罪名條列之，曰三尺須知錄，刊布於眾，俾民無誤罹法。

translations.literal: He extracted from the statutes and precedents the offenses commonly committed among the people and listed them in a work called Records of What the People Must Know, published it widely, and thereby kept the people from unwittingly violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the statutes' common offenses into a handbook called Records of What the People Must Know, published it widely, and helped common people avoid unwitting violations of the law.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷雲南布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 上以之望親老，調湖北，俾便迎養。

translations.literal: Because Zhiwang's parents were elderly, the emperor transferred him to Hubei so that he might more conveniently support them.
translations.idiomatic: Because his parents were elderly, the emperor moved him to Hubei so he could care for them more easily.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，教匪起荊、襄，蔓延鄖、宜、施南諸郡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing sectarian rebels rose in Jing and Xiang, spreading through the prefectures of Yun, Yi, and Shinan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796 White Lotus rebels broke out in Jing and Xiang and spread through Yun, Yi, and the Shinan region.

sentences.zh: 總督巡撫皆統師出，之望一人留武昌治事，訛言數作，時獲賊諜，偽檄遍通衢。

translations.literal: The governor-general and governors all took command of armies and went out; Zhiwang alone remained at Wuchang to manage affairs. Rumors arose repeatedly, rebel spies were captured from time to time, and forged proclamations were posted throughout the streets.
translations.idiomatic: While the governor-general and governors marched out with the armies, Zhiwang alone stayed at Wuchang to run the province. Rumors flared, rebel agents were caught, and forged proclamations appeared on every street.

sentences.zh: 之望靜定不驚，防禦要隘，城鄉市鎮設保甲互稽，民心帖然。

translations.literal: Zhiwang remained calm and unalarmed, defended the key passes, and established mutual surveillance through baojia in cities, towns, and marketplaces; popular sentiment settled.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his composure, fortified the critical passes, and set up mutual surveillance through baojia in town and country until the people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 賊犯孝感，調師翦滅，下游五郡皆安堵。

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked Xiaogan, he shifted troops and wiped them out; the five downstream prefectures all returned to peace.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck Xiaogan, he moved troops and destroyed them, and the five downstream prefectures were secured.

sentences.zh: 詔以之望雖未與賊戰，坐鎮根本，武、漢無虞，嘉其功，賜花翎。

translations.literal: An edict said that although Zhiwang had not fought the rebels in person, by holding the base secure he had kept Wuhan free from alarm; his merit was praised and he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him for holding the rear secure though he had not fought in the field, keeping Wuhan safe, and awarded him the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二年，丁父憂，命留任素服治事。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered mourning for his father and was ordered to remain in office and conduct affairs in plain mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797, when his father died, he was ordered to remain in office and govern in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 四年，安襄鄖道胡齊崙侵餉事發，命之望察治，齊崙侵蝕餽送，轇轕猝不易究，上切責之，命解任來京。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the case of An-Xiang-Yun circuit intendant Hu Qilun's embezzlement of military pay came to light. Zhiwang was ordered to investigate. Qilun had embezzled supplies and transport funds; the tangle of accounts was suddenly hard to unravel. The emperor sharply rebuked him and ordered him relieved of office and summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 the embezzlement of army pay by Circuit Intendant Hu Qilun of An-Xiang-Yun came to light. Zhiwang was ordered to investigate, but Qilun's diversions of supplies and transport funds proved too tangled to sort out quickly. The emperor rebuked him sharply and ordered him relieved and summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 及讞定，之望坐徇庇降調。

translations.literal: When the judgment was finalized, Zhiwang was punished for shielding him and was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was decided, Zhiwang was demoted for having shielded him.

sentences.zh: 上知之望無染指，居官有聲，素諳刑名，以按察使降補。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Zhiwang had not dipped his hand into the funds, that in office he had a good reputation, and that he was long versed in criminal law; he was demoted and reappointed as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had taken nothing for himself, had a strong reputation, and was expert in criminal law, the emperor reappointed him at the lower rank of judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 踰月，授刑部侍郎，予假葬父省母。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and granted leave to bury his father and visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made vice minister of punishments and granted leave to bury his father and visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 五年，授湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 he was appointed governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 鎮筸黑苗出峒焚掠，蔓延三廳，遣兵擊平之。

translations.literal: The Black Miao of Zhenqian came out of their stockades to burn and plunder, spreading through the three subprefectures; he sent troops and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Black Miao from Zhenqian raided out of the hills and spread through three subprefectures, he sent troops and put the rising down.

sentences.zh: 親勘常德堤圍私墾洲地百數十處，造冊立案，永息爭端。

translations.literal: He personally surveyed more than a hundred places in Changde where dikes had been encircled and sandbars privately reclaimed, made registers and established cases on file, and thereby ended disputes permanently.
translations.idiomatic: He personally surveyed more than a hundred illegal embankment enclosures around Changde, registered them, and settled the disputes for good.

sentences.zh: 尋復召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again recalled as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled again as vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 至京，面陳永綏廳孤懸苗境，不足資控制，請移廳治花園，移協營茶洞，沿邊遍設碉卡，以永綏舊城為汛地，使苗弁駐闉，約束諸苗寨，下所司議行。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he stated in audience that Yongshui Subprefecture stood isolated in the Miao country and was inadequate for control; he requested moving the subprefectural seat to Huayuan, moving the garrison brigade to Chadong, setting watchtowers and checkpoints all along the border, using the old Yongshui city as a garrison post, and stationing Miao officers in the walled town to restrain the Miao stockades. The matter was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In Beijing he argued in audience that Yongshui Subprefecture, isolated in the Miao country, could not hold the frontier. He proposed moving the seat to Huayuan, shifting the garrison to Chadong, building blockhouses along the border, turning the old Yongshui town into a garrison post, and posting Miao officers there to control the stockades. The court referred his plan to the responsible offices for action.

sentences.zh: 六年，偕侍郎那彥寶勘近畿水災，又偕侍郎高杞監疏長辛店河道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, together with Vice Minister Nayinbao, he surveyed flood damage in the capital region; together with Vice Minister Gao Qi he supervised dredging of the Changxindian river channel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he joined Vice Minister Nayinbao to inspect flood damage near the capital, and Vice Minister Gao Qi to supervise dredging at Changxindian.

sentences.zh: 七年，命赴山東按皁役之孫冒考，巡撫和瑛誣斷事，和瑛譴罷，即授之望巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to go to Shandong to investigate a yamen runner's grandson who had fraudulently taken the examination. Governor Hewang had wrongly decided the case; Hewang was rebuked and dismissed, and Zhiwang was immediately appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he was sent to Shandong to investigate a runner's grandson who had taken the exams fraudulently. Governor Hewang had misjudged the case, was dismissed, and Zhiwang was appointed governor in his place.

sentences.zh: 尋調陝西。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 大軍剿南山餘孽，之望籌備軍食，安插鄉勇，撫卹災黎，偕總督惠齡奏籌善後事宜甚悉。

translations.literal: As the great army suppressed the remnant rebels in the southern hills, Zhiwang prepared military provisions, settled local militia, and relieved disaster victims; together with Governor-General Huiling he memorialized in great detail on plans for postwar arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: While the main forces suppressed rebel remnants in the southern hills, he provisioned the army, settled local militia, and relieved the afflicted. With Governor-General Huiling he submitted a thorough plan for reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 調廣東，乞假省親。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong and requested leave to visit his family.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangdong, he asked for leave to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 九年，仍授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 he was again made vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 逾一年，以母老乞養歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year, citing his mother's age, he requested leave to support her and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, pleading his mother's age, he asked to retire and care for her at home.

sentences.zh: 十四年，仁宗五旬萬壽，之望入都祝嘏。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the Renzong Emperor's fiftieth-birthday celebration, Zhiwang entered the capital to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1809, for Jiaqing's fiftieth-birthday celebration, he came to Beijing to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 其母年八十有三，上垂問褒嘉，賚予有加。

translations.literal: His mother was eighty-three years old; the emperor inquired after her with praise and bestowed gifts with special generosity.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was eighty-three. The emperor asked after her with praise and gave her especially generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，服闋，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died and mourning ended, he was promoted to minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以病解職，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he left office because of illness and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he resigned because of illness and soon died.

sentences.zh: 韓崶，字桂舲，江蘇元和人。

translations.literal: Han Feng, courtesy name Guiling, was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Feng, whose courtesy name was Guiling, came from Yuanhe in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父是升，客遊京師，授經諸王邸，以名德稱。

translations.literal: His father Han Shisheng traveled to the capital as a guest, taught the classics in princely mansions, and was known for moral reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Shisheng had lived in Beijing as a guest scholar, teaching the classics in princely households and earning a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 崶少慧能文，由拔貢授刑部七品小京官，累擢郎中。

translations.literal: Feng was clever in youth and skilled in writing. From selected tribute student status he was appointed a seventh-rank junior secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and was promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and literary from youth, he entered the Ministry of Punishments as a junior secretary through the tribute-student selection and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十四年，出為河南彰德知府，遷廣東高廉道。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong he went out as prefect of Zhangde in Henan and was transferred to the Gaolian circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1789 he was posted as prefect of Zhangde in Henan, then transferred to the Gaolian circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 坐失察吳川知縣庇縱私鹽事，降刑部主事，复洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: Because he failed to detect that the Wuchuan magistrate had sheltered illegal private salt trade, he was reduced to principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, then was again promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments for failing to uncover a Wuchuan magistrate's protection of illegal salt smuggling, then rose again to director.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，授湖南嶽常澧道，遷按察使，調福建，署布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he was appointed to the Yue-Chang-Li circuit in Hunan, was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner, was transferred to Fujian, and served as acting provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he was made intendant of the Yue-Chang-Li circuit in Hunan, promoted to judicial commissioner, transferred to Fujian, and acted as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 蔡牽方擾台灣，海疆多事，崶籌軍備杜接濟甚力，遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: Cai Qian's faction was disturbing Taiwan and the maritime frontier was troubled; Feng worked hard to prepare military supplies and cut off their support, and was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: With Cai Qian's pirates troubling Taiwan and the coast in turmoil, he worked hard to ready defenses and cut off their supplies, and was made provincial treasurer of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was recalled as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1806 he was recalled as vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 十二年，命赴荊州按將軍積拉堪與知府交結事，又命勘南河。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was ordered to go to Jingzhou to investigate collusion between General Jilakan and the prefect, and was also ordered to survey the Southern Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1807 he was sent to Jingzhou to investigate collusion between General Jilakan and the prefect, and also to survey the Southern Canal.

sentences.zh: 十三年，宗室敏學恃勢不法，讞擬輕比，詔斥部臣屈法縱姦，譴責有差。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the imperial clansman Min Xue relied on his status and acted unlawfully; the proposed judgment used a lenient analogy. An edict rebuked the ministry officials for bending the law to indulge wrongdoing, and rebukes were assigned in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In 1808 the imperial clansman Min Xue abused his status and broke the law, yet the ministry proposed a lenient sentence. The throne rebuked the officials for bending the law to protect him, and punished them in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 崶方奉使河間讞獄，未與畫諾，上以崶先於召對面陳，意存開脫，且部事素由崶先覈定，跡近專擅，降授廣東按察使。

translations.literal: Feng was at the time on mission in Hejian reviewing criminal cases and had not countersigned the proposal. The emperor held that Feng had earlier stated in audience his intent to secure leniency, and that ministry affairs had long been pre-approved by Feng first, which looked like usurpation of authority; he was demoted and appointed Guangdong provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was away in Hejian reviewing cases and had not countersigned the proposal. The emperor believed he had already signaled leniency in audience and had long pre-approved ministry business himself—conduct that looked like overreach—and demoted him to judicial commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利兵船佔澳門砲台，入黃埔，久之始退。

translations.literal: At that time English warships occupied the Macao batteries, entered Whampoa, and only after a long time withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At that time British warships seized the Macao batteries, entered Whampoa, and withdrew only after a long standoff.

sentences.zh: 總督吳熊光不即遣兵驅逐，以罪罷，命崶兼署總督。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Xiongguang did not immediately send troops to drive them off; for this offense he was dismissed, and Feng was ordered to serve additionally as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Xiongguang had not sent troops at once to expel them and was dismissed. Feng was ordered to act additionally as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十四年，崶查閱澳門夷民安堵，因疏陳：「西洋人於其地舊設砲台六，請自伽思蘭砲台迤南，加築女牆二百餘丈，於前山寨駐專營，蓮花莖增關徬石垣，新湧山口築砲台，填蕉門海口，以資控制。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Feng inspected Macao and found the foreign residents settled in peace. In a memorial he stated: "Westerners have long maintained six batteries there. From the Jiasilan battery southward, please add more than two hundred zhang of parapet wall, station a dedicated garrison at Qianshan Stockade, add stone walls at the passes of Lianhuajing, build a battery at Xinyong Hill Pass, and fill in the Jiaomen estuary to aid control."
translations.idiomatic: In 1809, finding Macao's foreign residents at peace, he memorialized: "The Westerners maintain six batteries there. From Jiasilan southward, add two hundred-odd zhang of parapet, post a dedicated garrison at Qianshan, strengthen the Lianhuajing passes with stone walls, build a battery at Xinyong Hill Pass, and fill the Jiaomen estuary to tighten control."

sentences.zh: 」如議行。

translations.literal: This was adopted as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 又密陳粵海形勢：「沿海村落，處處可通，外洋盜匪，易生窺伺。

translations.literal: He also secretly memorialized on the situation in the Guangdong seas: "Along the coast every village offers access; overseas pirates can easily spy out opportunities."
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a confidential memorial on the Guangdong coast: "Every coastal village offers a passage inland, and overseas pirates can easily probe for openings."

sentences.zh: 必先固內而後可禦外。

translations.literal: The interior must first be secured before the exterior can be defended.
translations.idiomatic: The interior must be secured before the coast can be defended.

sentences.zh: 凡屬扼要砲台，宜簡練精銳，嚴密防守。

translations.literal: All strategic batteries should select and train elite troops and defend them strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Every key battery should be manned by picked, well-trained troops under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 並令沿海紳衿耆董，督率丁壯，互相捍護，自衛身家，較為得力。

translations.literal: Coastal gentry, elders, and community heads should also be ordered to lead able-bodied men in mutual defense to protect their own households; this would be more effective.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal gentry and elders should also be ordered to lead local men in mutual defense of their homes; that would be more effective.

sentences.zh: 」百齡繼為總督，會奏：「華、洋交易章程，外國兵船停泊外洋，澳內華、洋人分別稽覈。

translations.literal: When Bailin succeeded as governor-general, they jointly memorialized: "Regulations for Chinese and foreign trade: foreign warships are to anchor in the outer seas; within Macao Chinese and foreigners are to be checked separately."
translations.idiomatic: When Bailin became governor-general, they jointly proposed trade rules: foreign warships were to anchor offshore, and Chinese and foreigners in Macao were to be inspected separately.

sentences.zh: 各國商賈，止許暫留司事之人，經理債務，餘俱飭依期回國，不得在澳逗留。

translations.literal: Merchants of every nation may leave only those who manage affairs temporarily to settle debts; all others are to be ordered to return home on schedule and may not linger in Macao.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign merchants might leave only clerks to settle accounts; all others were to return home on schedule and not remain in Macao.

sentences.zh: 洋船引水人，責令澳門同知給發牌照。

translations.literal: Pilots for foreign ships are to be licensed by order of the Macao subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign-ship pilots were to be licensed by the Macao subprefect.

sentences.zh: 買辦等華人，責成地方有司慎選承充，隨時稽察。

translations.literal: Chinese compradors and the like are to be carefully selected and appointed by local officials, who are responsible for inspecting them at all times.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese compradors were to be carefully chosen by local officials and inspected at all times.

sentences.zh: 洋船起貨時，不許洋商私自分撥。

translations.literal: When foreign ships unload cargo, foreign merchants are not permitted to distribute goods privately.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign ships unloaded cargo, merchants were forbidden to distribute goods on their own.

sentences.zh: 」下軍機大臣採擇議行。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Grand Council ministers to select provisions and implement them.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council was ordered to select provisions and put them into effect.

sentences.zh: 逾年，海盜張保仔就撫，烏石二、東海霸以次誅降，賜花翎。

translations.literal: After more than a year the pirate Zhang Bao'er accepted pacification; Wushi Er, Dong Haiba, and others were executed or surrendered in turn, and Feng was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the pirate Zhang Bao'er submitted to pacification; Wushi Er, Dong Haiba, and others were killed or surrendered in turn, and Feng was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十六年，复署總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he again served as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1811 he again acted as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 疏請免米稅，以通商販、裕民食。

translations.literal: In a memorial he requested exemption of the rice tax to promote trade and ease the people's food supply.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish the rice tax so trade could flow and the people's food supply would ease.

sentences.zh: 又疏陳：「潮州多械鬥，而營員無協緝之責，請令文武會拏；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Chaozhou has many armed affrays, yet garrison officers have no duty to assist in arrest; please order civil and military officials to seize offenders jointly."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed: "Chaozhou suffers many armed feuds, yet garrison officers are not required to help arrest offenders. Let civil and military officials seize them jointly."

sentences.zh: 距省遠，請軍流以下就近由巡道覆覈。

translations.literal: Because the distance from the provincial capital is great, he requested that cases below military exile be reviewed nearby by circuit intendants.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region lies far from the provincial capital, he asked that sentences below military exile be reviewed locally by circuit intendants.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「懲治悍匪，請如四川例：初犯械系，限一年改行；

translations.literal: He also said: "In punishing violent criminals, please follow the Sichuan precedent: on a first offense they are shackled and given one year to reform their conduct."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, for punishing violent offenders, following the Sichuan precedent: first offenders were to be shackled and given one year to reform.

sentences.zh: 積兩限如故，即治以棍徒屢次滋擾律。

translations.literal: If after two such terms their conduct is unchanged, they are to be punished under the statute on ruffians who repeatedly cause disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: If they failed to reform after two such terms, they were to be punished under the statute on habitual troublemakers.

sentences.zh: 」皆允行。

translations.literal: All were approved and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 十八年，入覲，授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he came to court audience and was appointed minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he attended court audience and was appointed minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 崶父是升年八十，給假三月歸為壽。

translations.literal: Feng's father Shisheng was eighty years old; he was granted three months' leave to return home and celebrate his birthday.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shisheng was eighty; he was granted three months' leave to go home and celebrate his birthday.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，丁父憂，服闋，以一品銜署刑部侍郎，尋補刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he entered mourning for his father; when the mourning period ended he served with first-rank insignia as acting vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, and soon afterward was appointed regular minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1816, after his father's death and mourning, he served as acting vice minister of punishments with first-rank insignia and soon became regular minister.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，平反山西榆次縣民閻思虎獄，被議敘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he reversed the wrongful conviction of Yan Sihu, a commoner of Yuci County in Shanxi, and was recommended for merit promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he reversed the wrongful conviction of Yan Sihu of Yuci County, Shanxi, and was recommended for a merit citation.

sentences.zh: 初，思虎強姦趙二姑，知縣呂錫齡受賕，逼認和姦，趙二姑忿而自盡，親屬京控。

translations.literal: At first Sihu had raped Zhao Ergu; Magistrate Lü Xiling accepted a bribe and forced her to confess to consensual illicit intercourse. Zhao Ergu, enraged, hanged herself, and her relatives appealed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Sihu had raped Zhao Ergu. Magistrate Lü Xiling took a bribe and forced her to confess to consensual adultery. Enraged, she killed herself, and her family appealed to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 命巡撫親提，仍以和姦擬結。

translations.literal: The governor was ordered to conduct a personal reexamination, yet still concluded the case as consensual illicit intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: The governor was ordered to retry the case in person, yet still concluded it was consensual adultery.

sentences.zh: 御史梁中靖疏劾，提解刑部，審得實情是強非和，並原審各官賄囑、徇縱、回護諸弊狀，思虎論斬，趙二姑旌表，巡撫邱樹棠、按察使盧元偉及府縣各官，降革遣戍有差。

translations.literal: Censor Liang Zhongjing memorialized in impeachment; the case was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments. The facts were found to be rape and not consensual intercourse, and all the abuses of the original trial officials were established, including bribery, favoritism, and cover-up. Sihu was sentenced to decapitation; Zhao Ergu was granted posthumous honor; Governor Qiu Shutang, Judicial Commissioner Lu Yuanwei, and the prefectural and county officials were demoted, dismissed, or exiled in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liang Zhongjing impeached the officials. The case went to the Ministry of Punishments, which found rape rather than consensual adultery and exposed bribery, favoritism, and cover-up in the original trial. Sihu was sentenced to death; Zhao Ergu was posthumously honored; Governor Qiu Shutang, Judicial Commissioner Lu Yuanwei, and the lower officials were demoted, dismissed, or exiled in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉刑部堂司各官秉公申雪，並予議敘。

translations.literal: An edict praised the ministry's senior and bureau officials for upholding justice and clearing the wrong, and granted them consideration for merit promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised the ministry's senior officials for vindicating the victim fairly and recommended them for merit citations.

sentences.zh: 梁中靖參奏得實，亦加四品銜。

translations.literal: Liang Zhongjing's impeachment was found accurate, and he too was given fourth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhongjing's impeachment was upheld, and he too received fourth-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 會有官犯侯際清擬流，呈請贖罪，部議因際清犯罪情重，仍以可否並請。

translations.literal: At the same time the official offender Hou Jiqing was sentenced to exile, and a request was submitted to redeem his punishment. The ministry, because Jiqing's offense was grave, still submitted the question of approval or disapproval together.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time the official offender Hou Jiqing was sentenced to exile and petitioned to redeem his punishment. Because his offense was grave, the ministry still referred the question of approval to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔斥含混取巧，命大學士托津等查訊，侍郎恩銘、常英、司員恩德等皆有賄囑情事，崶亦解任就質，坐失察司員得賄，嗣子知情，親屬撞騙，議奪職遣戍，因年老，從寬，命效力萬年吉地工程處。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked this as evasive trickery and ordered Grand Secretary Tuojin and others to investigate. Vice Ministers Enming and Chang Ying, and secretary En De and others all had bribery connections. Feng was also removed from office to give testimony. He was punished for failing to detect that a secretary had taken bribes, for his son's knowledge of it, and for relatives' extortion by false claims; dismissal and exile were proposed. Because of his age leniency was shown, and he was ordered to serve at the Wannian auspicious-site construction office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne denounced this as evasive trickery and ordered Grand Secretary Tuojin to investigate. Vice Ministers Enming and Chang Ying and Secretary En De were all implicated in bribery. Feng was removed to give testimony, punished for failing to detect a secretary's bribes, his son's knowledge of them, and relatives' fraud, and recommended for dismissal and exile. Because of his age he was spared and sent to serve at the imperial mausoleum construction office.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，召署刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled to serve as acting vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was recalled as acting vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病乞歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he requested retirement because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he retired because of illness.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1834 he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：有清一代，於刑部用人最慎。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Throughout the Qing dynasty, appointments to the Ministry of Punishments were made with the greatest care.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Throughout the Qing, appointments to the Ministry of Punishments were made with exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 凡總辦秋審，必擇司員明慎習故事者為之。

translations.literal: Those who directed the autumn review of capital cases were always chosen from secretaries who were clear-minded, cautious, and versed in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of the autumn capital-case review were always chosen from secretaries who were careful, prudent, and steeped in precedent.

sentences.zh: 或出為監司數年，稍迴翔疆圻，入掌邦憲，輒終其身，故多能盡職。

translations.literal: Some served several years as provincial supervisors, moved briefly through frontier posts, then entered to head the national penal code and often remained for life; therefore most were able to fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Some served years as provincial supervisors, passed briefly through frontier posts, then entered to head the penal code and often kept the post for life; most therefore performed their duties well.

sentences.zh: 仁宗尤留意刑獄，往往親裁，所用部臣，斯其選也。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor paid special attention to criminal cases and often decided them personally; the ministry officials he used were chosen accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing paid special attention to criminal justice and often decided cases himself; the ministry officials he used were chosen with that in mind.

sentences.zh: 姜晟、祖之望，易攵歷中外，並有政績。

translations.literal: Jiang Cheng and Zu Zhiwang served in posts both within the capital and in the provinces and both had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cheng and Zu Zhiwang served widely in the capital and provinces and both left solid records of governance.

sentences.zh: 金光悌、韓崶，皆筦部務最久，光悌治事尤厲鋒鍔，號刻深雲。

translations.literal: Jin Guangti and Han Feng both managed ministry affairs the longest; Guangti in handling affairs was especially sharp and unyielding, and was known as harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guangti and Han Feng both managed ministry affairs the longest. Guangti was especially sharp and unyielding in office and was known as harsh and severe.
